recommendations.rationale: To satisfy the user contract goal of cutting infrastructure spend while sustaining everyday load (100-200 users), downsizing from t3.medium (2 vCPU, 4 GiB) to t3.small (2 vCPU, 2 GiB) is recommended. At 100 users, CPU max is 43.722% and peak RAM usage is 1674113024.0 bytes (~1.56 GiB). At 200 users, CPU max reaches 69.011% and peak RAM usage is 1677516800.0 bytes (~1.56 GiB). Because t3.small maintains 2 vCPUs and provides 2 GiB of memory, it supports normal operating conditions at a lower cost. However, metrics show initial peak RAM reached 2028228608.0 bytes (~1.89 GiB) at 10 users, meaning memory headroom will be constrained on a 2 GiB instance under burst conditions.

overall_assessment: The system can be downsized from t3.medium to t3.small to meet the primary objective of reducing compute expenditure while sustaining everyday user concurrency (100-200 users). At 200 users, max CPU utilization is 69.011% and RAM usage peaks at 1677516800.0 bytes (~1.56 GiB), which fits within t3.small's 2 vCPU / 2 GiB allocation. Note that at higher loads (500+ users) CPU max reaches 99.744%, so this smaller sizing will not accommodate heavy peak traffic without latency degradation, aligned with the contract's explicit trade-off prioritizing cost reduction over peak capacity.
